qt: to the Commission Konstantinos Arvanitis (The Left) Subject:

Spotify provides access to podcasts, audiobooks, public playlists and associated text, images and video supplied by users and professional creators. It recommends and disseminates that content through algorithmic systems and monetises user attention through subscriptions and advertising. Spotify itself treats Spotify Main, Spotify for Creators, Spotify for Artists and Spotify for Authors as intermediary services under the Digital Services Act (DSA). Its latest figures report 751 million monthly active users globally, with growth in Europe. Nevertheless, Spotify is absent from the Commission’s list of designated very large online platforms (VLOPs). Under Articles 3(i), 3(p) and 33 DSA, services disseminating recipient-supplied information to the public must be designated as VLOPs when they have at least 45 million average monthly active recipients in the EU. Given Spotify’s scale, recommender systems and capacity to amplify podcasts and other content affecting public discourse, consumer protection and fundamental rights: 1.
Has the Commission assessed whether Spotify’s relevant intermediary services constitute online platforms and exceed the Article 33 threshold?
Has it requested service-specific EU recipient data from Spotify under Article 24(3) DSA, including recipients exposed to creator-uploaded content through Spotify Main?
If the conditions are satisfied, will the Commission designate the relevant Spotify services as VLOPs, and if not, will it publish its legal and quantitative reasons for not doing so?
at: (English version) to the Commission Konstantinos Arvanitis (The Left) (4 September 2026) Subject: Possible designation of Spotify as a very large online platform under the Digital Services Act Spotify provides access to podcasts, audiobooks, public playlists and associated text, images and video supplied by users and professional creators. It recommends and disseminates that content through algorithmic systems and monetises user attention through subscriptions and advertising. (10 November 2026) Under the Digital Services Act (DSA) (1), the Commission has been assessing the qualification as very large online platform (VLOP) and very large online search engine (VLOSE) of services that are online platforms and online search engines and reach 45 million average monthly active recipients in the EU. So far, the Commission has adopted decisions designating 28 VLOPs and VLOSEs (2). Spotify has significantly evolved in terms of features, dissemination of third-party content and in users over the past years. The Commission has been closely following this evolution in coordination with the responsible Digital Services Coordinator, the Swedish Post and Telecom Authority, Post- och telestyrelsen. The Commission has taken note of Spotify's publications and is examining all information available to it. As part of this assessment, the Commission has engaged with representatives of the provider of Spotify, including through requests for information in May 2023 and in January 2026 to which Spotify responded. At present, the Commission continues to evaluate the (potential) qualification of Spotify as a VLOP. A potential conclusion that Spotify does not meet the article 33 DSA threshold will not be published.

Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 19 October 2022 on a Single Market For Digital Services and amending Directive 2000/31/EC (Digital Services Act). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2022/2065/oj. Supervision of the designated very large online platforms and search engines under DSA — https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/list-designatedvlops-and-vloses.
